# 1 Clement Chapter 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_011_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 11

**11:1** Because of his hospitality and piety, Lot was saved out of Sodom, when all the surrounding region was judged by fire and brimstone; the Lord making manifest that he does not forsake those who hope in him, but delivers to punishment and torment those who are other-minded. [Gen 19]

**11:2** For a sign of this his wife was left behind, because, since her soul was not in one accord nor in agreement with him, she became a pillar of salt unto this day, that it might be made known to all that the double-minded and those who doubt the power of God fall under judgment and become a warning to all generations. [Gen 19:26]

---

*EMET: "double-minded" (*dipsuchos*) — a word used prominently in James 1:8; 4:8. The Lot story becomes a homily on doubt and irreversibility of God's judgment.*
